content_voiceover: This slide compares the two major staging systems for CLL, the Rai system and the Binet system. The Rai system ranges from stage zero to stage four. Stage zero is lymphocytosis alone, with lymphocytes over fifteen thousand per microliter in blood and more than forty percent lymphocytes in the bone marrow, and it's low risk. Stage one adds enlarged lymph nodes, and stage two adds splenomegaly or hepatomegaly, both intermediate risk. Stage three adds anemia with hemoglobin below eleven, and stage four adds thrombocytopenia with platelets below one hundred thousand, both of these are high risk categories. The Binet system uses three groups, A, B, and C, based on hemoglobin, platelet count, and the number of enlarged lymphoid areas. Group A has fewer than three enlarged areas with normal hemoglobin and platelets. Group B has three or more enlarged areas but still normal counts. Group C is defined by hemoglobin below ten or platelets below one hundred thousand, regardless of how many areas are involved. For boards, remember that anemia or thrombocytopenia defines the high risk group in both systems.
keypoints: Rai stage zero to four, based on lymphocytosis, nodes, organomegaly, cytopenias
Binet A to C, based on hemoglobin, platelets, and node areas
Anemia or thrombocytopenia signals high risk in either system
Rai stage three-four and Binet C are the high risk categories
keypoint_voiceover: Two systems, same idea. Rai stage three or four and Binet stage C both mean anemia or thrombocytopenia is present, marking high risk disease. Lower stages are based purely on lymphocytosis, nodal involvement, and organomegaly without cytopenias.
